_comment: Single style source for every CloudLabs deliverable (decision Hans 3 Jul 2026: Calibri 10.5, five-level palette). JSON so both the python docengine and PowerShell (ConvertFrom-Json) read the same file natively. Change values here, never in builder code.

Vocabulary._comment: Taxonomy vocabulary control block. Languages is the authoritative language list: the validator requires every severity, scope, coverage and verdict value in every language named here, so adding a fourth language is one entry plus one set of label entries, with no resolver, renderer or layout change. Version moves with the catalogue: a vocabulary release and a catalogue release are the same release (see docs/Taxonomy-Vocabulary.md). PrimaryLanguage is the language authored prose is written in when a register does not say, which is every register written before content became multilingual. It is a fact of its own and NOT the first entry of DeliveryLanguages: reordering the delivery list would otherwise silently reinterpret every existing register as carrying a language nobody wrote in it. ReviewedLanguages (issue 271, section 6 punt 3) is a language a real reviewer can check a translation into - a DIFFERENT question from DeliveryLanguages (are the labels and catalogue complete): a language can be technically deliverable and still have nobody who can review a translation into it, and promoting it to DeliveryLanguages without also adding it here is a measured error (tests/multilingual_checks.py m31).

LanguageCodes._comment: How a language is written in a FILENAME. A separate fact from the language name, and deliberately so: a register key is read by a human editing JSON, where 'English' is clearer than 'en', while a filename suffix has to be short and stable. Both live here, so neither is invented at a call site. A rendered artifact carries its language because that is part of what the file IS, not as a uniqueness trick: a delta document for one measurement in two languages is two deliverables and must read as two, so the code is part of the name.

DoNotTranslate._comment: Terms that must read identically in every language. Enforced is checked mechanically across the whole label surface by the vocabulary validator. ProseOnly holds generic technical nouns that are do-not-translate in AUTHORED PROSE (remediation texts, findings, annotations) but ARE legitimately localised in the label surface, where NODE renders as Knoten in German; enforcing them there would forbid a correct translation.
_AsBuiltComment: Labels that read IDENTICALLY in Dutch and English on the as-built surface, and
are meant to. Product names (Windows Admin Center, Cluster-Aware Updating,
Storage Spaces Direct), technology terms (VLAN, MTU, RDMA, LAG, NOS, RPO) and
nouns that are the same word in both languages (Node, Model, Status, Interface).
IT IS AN INVENTORY, NOT A PROHIBITION (6 aug 2026). Before this, 134 as-built
labels were identical in both languages and NONE was recorded as deliberate, so
an intended English term and a forgotten translation looked exactly alike. This
list freezes the 134; the 135th has to be added on purpose, and the check in
tests/asbuilt_content_checks.py refuses an untidy new one.
MEASURED VALUES ARE NOT IN SCOPE HERE and never will be. What a system reported
is rendered as it reported it: an English event text, service state or product
string from an English-language OS stays English in a Dutch document, because
translating a measured value would be changing the measurement.

Risk._comment: Severity colour tokens, and only severity: how bad a finding is. ONE palette since 28 Jul 2026 and one SET of tokens since decision E2 (29 Jul 2026): the document and the Studio carry these same four values on every surface, with no dark/light variant, because they are read side by side and the same colour meaning two levels is a misreading an assessor can make. E2 reversed the ramp rather than tuning it: KRITIEK is black, which is the one value that is unmistakable on a white page and on the dark cockpit alike, and the level below it takes the red. That black cannot stand out on a dark surface, so it carries a ring; see Styles.RiskRing. Re-balanced 26 Jul 2026 to make room for KRITIEK above HOOG. OPGELOST, GEEN and n.v.t. left this block at 0.47 with the status axis; the first two are in Styles.Status, n.v.t. was dropped because the coverage group already carries not-applicable. Documents rendered before a change keep their old colours until they are re-rendered.

RiskRing._comment: Ring colour per severity, for the levels that have one. Only KRITIEK does, and the ring is what makes its black fill visible on a dark surface (1.18 against the cockpit; the ring is 5.01 there and 5.92 against the fill itself). It is a component rule of the badge and not a fourth colour in the ramp, which is why it lives in its own block: a level named here has a ring, a level absent has none, and the check that accepts KRITIEK's fill contrast does so ONLY where the ring is present and itself clears the floor. Applies to the severity badge and to the board dot, in every output channel.

Status._comment: Status colour tokens: where a finding stands, independently of what it is worth. OPEN carries the 'inherit' sentinel because an open finding's badge shows the colour of its severity; the sentinel is declared rather than left out so the rule stays 'every value has a token'. The validator accepts it on OPEN and refuses it anywhere else. GEEN is green because no deviation is a good state; ACCEPTED is neutral grey because a knowingly carried risk is neither cleared nor open. NOTE: GEEN was grey 7F7F7F while it was a severity value, so a re-rendered report changes that badge from grey to green.

RiskLabels._comment: Severity badge labels. Machine values are Dutch and never change (KRITIEK, HOOG, MIDDEL, LAAG); only the rendered label localises. KRITIEK: availability or data protection is compromised now, or failure is certain under normal operation. Tiebreaker against HOOG: does this break failover today? If yes, KRITIEK. If only under a specific trigger, HOOG. Where a finding STANDS is StatusLabels, a separate group since 0.47.

StatusLabels._comment: Status badge labels, upper case like RiskLabels because they share the badge surface. Machine values are Dutch except ACCEPTED, which entered the registers in English and stays; its Dutch label is GEACCEPTEERD. ACCEPTED never renders as solved: they are opposite statements about the same risk.

StatusNotes._comment: The status as a NOTE under a finding title, lower case and muted, instead of a badge beside the severity. A badge column that carries GEACCEPTEERD next to one that carries MIDDEL presents level and state as before and after of one thing, which is the axis conflation removed from the registers, the renderer, the delta report and the cockpit; this block is what replaces it. OPEN is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: an open finding's state is already said by the severity badge on the same row, so a note there would repeat it. The other three are present in every declared language, resolved like every other label and never hardcoded in a renderer. The wording is not the badge label lower-cased: GEEN reads as 'geen' on its own, which says nothing, and the note has to be a statement.

ConfirmNote._comment: The bulk-confirmation note, per language (issue 301). It is MACHINE TEXT with a fixed template - the studio writes it, no assessor types it - so it belongs in the layer beside AcceptanceNote rather than in a Dutch string in studio/shell.py. That distinction is the whole point: authored assessor prose is never machine-translated, and this is not authored prose. {run} is the round key. The Assessor prefix is the same word in all three languages (docs/Duitse-Terminologie.md settles assessor -> Assessor) and lives here so no caller spells it out. TranslationReviewed is the naleesronde's own note (issue 301, 19 aug 2026), and it is here for exactly the reason Bulk is: Confirm-TranslatedText.ps1 wrote it as a plain Dutch string, so reviewing the German halves was the very act that made the German render refuse with "history note is a plain string". {language} is the half that was read, {source} the language it was translated from, {who} the person who read it - the reviewer's NAME is data, not text to translate. TranslationReviewedBulk is the SAME act taken over many halves at once (Hans, 19 aug 2026): the reviewer accepts a batch on the strength of the translation chain rather than reading every line. It is a different sentence on purpose - a record that says 'read' about halves nobody read line by line makes check 20 green without meaning, and the bulk value confirmation has named itself for exactly this reason since issue 301. DE SAMMEL-FAMILIE EN NIET 'im Stapel' (batch 7 op #413, 19 aug): 'Stapel' leest in het Duits als een fysieke stapel of oude batchverwerking. Deze zinnen worden als MOMENTOPNAME in registernoten geschreven, dus een latere laagveeg heelt ze niet - daarom hier meteen goed. THE REGISTER RULE FOR THE NEXT TEMPLATE WRITER (R1, issue 561/575, 22 Aug 2026): Bulk is a MACHINE STAMP on many findings at once and stays telegram-style, never expanded into a full sentence describing an action - there is no action to describe, only a value that did not move. TranslationReviewed and TranslationReviewedBulk are full sentences because they report something a PERSON did (read a translation, or accepted a batch of them on the strength of the chain). The register is not accidental: pick telegram for a machine stamp, a full sentence for a human act, and it is the same choice every field in this block already makes.

AcceptanceNote._comment: The Status line of a borne risk, built from the ACCEPTANCE RECORD and not from the last history note. It used to be the note, which is why accepted findings read 'Assessor: <reason> [run 20260728]': a machine word the customer never asked for, a run key that answers nothing at that point in the sentence, and no sign of who decided or when it is looked at again. The record carries By, On, Why and ReviewOn, so the sentence can say all four. An authored Status annotation still overrides this, because an assessor who writes the paragraph out has said something the record cannot hold. Standing and Dated are two templates and not one with an optional tail: 'no review date' is a decision and has to read as one, not as an absence. Why is a plain string typed at accept time and is NOT a language map, so it renders in the language it was typed in; that is the same limitation the history note always had, and it is visible here rather than hidden. Months are spelled out because an ISO date in a customer paragraph reads as a machine field.

ScopeLabels._comment: Scope answers what a finding says something about, so a single workload finding cannot set the severity of a cluster-wide verdict. Machine values are Dutch for consistency with the severity enum, except where the term is identical or already a loanword in Dutch technical usage. NODE versus CLUSTER follows the ownership principle: owned and remediated on one node is NODE, a component or path shared by all nodes is CLUSTER. WORKLOAD and BEHEER can never carry KRITIEK; their ceiling is HOOG and the vocabulary validator enforces it from SCOPE_KRITIEK_FORBIDDEN.

ScopeOverrides._comment: Module-family display overrides for a scope value: WORKLOAD reads poorly in a report that talks about virtual machines. Resolution is module override if present, otherwise the generic ScopeLabels entry. That is the one intended fallback in the system and it never crosses a language. Display only: the machine value stays WORKLOAD everywhere.

CoverageLabels._comment: Coverage state to report term. not-applicable renders as Not applicable; every skipped-* state AND collection-failed render as Not assessed. The two are never collapsed in stored data or in aggregate counts: skipped means we decided not to measure, collection-failed means the environment prevented measurement, and only the second is a signal about the environment itself.

_comment: A4, set explicitly (6 aug 2026). Nobody had ever set a page size, so every
document came out US Letter, which is what python-docx ships. On A4 the 5.9
inch tables and figures stuck 3.3 mm past the right margin, which is the few
millimetres that were visible. Side margins are 1.134 in so the usable width
stays exactly 6.0 in and no width in this file had to move.
room FigureWidthIn already takes off UsableWidthIn, applied to a LANDSCAPE
page instead - PageHeightIn minus two SideMarginIn minus 0.1 = 9.3. A
landscape page reuses the portrait page's own dimensions and margins
(swapped), so this is the only new number the landscape section needed.

Verdicts._comment: Comparer verdict to report rendering: which badge to show and the change-column text. Verdict tokens are language neutral; the per-language keys are the reader-facing phrases. The Change* labels in Styles.Labels carried a trailing (assessor) to mark a register decision apart from a machine verdict. It came off on 29 Jul 2026: the change text is now ALWAYS derived from the register axes and the machine verdict rides along in brackets only when it adds something, so the qualifier said nothing the sentence did not, appeared on 40 of 55 rows of a delivered table including every row where nothing happened, and produced two brackets in a row on the three rows where a verdict did ride along.

ASSESSOR-OVERRULE._comment: The machine proposed something and the assessor decided otherwise. The seventh measured verdict, 31 July 2026. Badge is null because the row's badge comes from the FINDING's value, which is exactly the thing the assessor decided; a badge here would restate the machine's proposal beside the decision that rejected it. The phrase names the DECISION and not the disagreement: 'assessorbesluit wijkt af van de machinelezing' would put the machine first, and the whole point is that the register is what stands. What the machine said is kept in its own field on the row and renders as the second line, so nothing is hidden.

MethodologyDefault: Elke bevinding volgt een vaste structuur: Huidige situatie, Best practice, Afwijking, Aanbeveling, Actiepunt en Referentie. De diepgang schaalt met het risico: hoog en middel krijgen alle onderdelen inclusief een concreet actiepunt, laag de kern (situatie, best practice, afwijking, aanbeveling), geen risico bevestigt wat is gemeten.

Kritiek: beschikbaarheid of gegevensbescherming is nu aangetast, of uitval is zeker bij normaal gebruik. Onderscheid met hoog: breekt dit vandaag de failover? Zo ja, kritiek. Alleen bij een specifieke trigger, hoog.
Hoog: dataverlies, ongeplande downtime, clusterinstabiliteit, niet-ondersteunde configuratie of eenvoudig uit te buiten security-blootstelling.

Middel: supportability-impact (Microsoft kan support weigeren), meetbare performance-degradatie, single points of failure die niet direct de uptime bedreigen, afwijking van vendor compatibility matrices.
Laag: hygiene, documentatielacunes, naam- en taginconsistenties, kleine inefficienties, cosmetische afwijkingen.
Geen risico / geen afwijking: conform best practice en nooit eerder een bevinding geweest, of inventarislacunes die buiten de huidige scope vallen.
Opgelost: een eerder vastgestelde bevinding waarvan het herstel in deze meting is gemeten; de historie (wanneer open, op welk niveau) blijft in het register zodat de voortgang meetbaar is.

MethodologyDefault: Each finding follows a fixed structure: Current situation, Best practice, Deviation, Recommendation, Action item and Reference. Depth scales with risk: high and medium carry every part including a concrete action item, low the core (situation, best practice, deviation, recommendation), no risk confirms what was measured.

Critical: availability or data protection is compromised now, or failure is certain under normal operation. Tiebreaker against high: does this break failover today? If yes, critical. If only under a specific trigger, high.
High: data loss, unplanned downtime, cluster instability, unsupported configuration or easily exploitable security exposure.

Medium: supportability impact (Microsoft can refuse support), measurable performance degradation, single points of failure that do not directly threaten uptime, deviation from vendor compatibility matrices.
Low: hygiene, documentation gaps, naming and tagging inconsistencies, minor inefficiencies, cosmetic deviations.
No risk / no deviation: conforms to best practice and was never a finding, or inventory gaps that fall outside the current scope.
Resolved: a previously established finding whose repair was measured in this run; the history (when open, at what level) stays in the register so progress is measurable.

German.IntroSummary: Dieser Delta-Abschnitt vergleicht die Messung vom {current} mit der vorherigen Messung vom {baseline}. Die Beurteilungen unten verteilen sich wie folgt: {counts}.

MethodologyDefault: Jede Feststellung folgt einem festen Aufbau: Aktuelle Situation, Best Practice, Abweichung, Empfehlung, Maßnahme und Referenz. Die Tiefe richtet sich nach dem Risiko: hoch und mittel tragen jeden Teil einschließlich einer konkreten Maßnahme, niedrig den Kern (Situation, Best Practice, Abweichung, Empfehlung), kein Risiko bestätigt das Gemessene.

Kritisch: Verfügbarkeit oder Datenschutz sind jetzt beeinträchtigt, oder ein Ausfall ist im Normalbetrieb sicher. Abgrenzung zu hoch: Bricht dies das Failover heute? Wenn ja, kritisch. Nur bei einem bestimmten Auslöser, dann hoch.
Hoch: Datenverlust, ungeplante Ausfallzeit, Clusterinstabilität, nicht unterstützte Konfiguration oder leicht ausnutzbare Sicherheitslücke.

Mittel: Auswirkung auf die Supportfähigkeit (Microsoft kann den Support verweigern), messbare Leistungseinbußen, Single Points of Failure, die die Verfügbarkeit nicht unmittelbar gefährden, Abweichung von den Kompatibilitätsmatrizen des Herstellers.
Niedrig: Hygiene, Dokumentationslücken, Inkonsistenzen bei Benennung und Tagging, kleinere Ineffizienzen, kosmetische Abweichungen.
Kein Risiko / keine Abweichung: entspricht der Best Practice und war nie eine Feststellung, oder Inventarlücken außerhalb des aktuellen Umfangs.
Behoben: eine zuvor erhobene Feststellung, deren Behebung in diesem Lauf gemessen wurde; die Historie (wann offen, auf welcher Stufe) bleibt im Register, damit der Fortschritt messbar bleibt.

RiskText._comment: TEXT variant of the severity colours, for a coloured WORD on white. Not a second palette and never a fill: the same value, made readable as text, which is why the block is named RiskText and not RiskAlt or RiskDark. A name that does not say 'text' gets used as a fill within the year and then there are two palettes again, which is what decision E2 abolished. Its own block for the same reason RiskRing has one: it is a component rule of a surface, not a colour in the ramp. WHY IT EXISTS: a filled badge carries white text and clears BADGE_CONTRAST_FLOOR at 3.0; a coloured word on white is a LABEL and has to clear LABEL_FLOOR at 4.5. Measured on the badge colours: KRITIEK 21.00 and HOOG 4.51 clear it, MIDDEL 3.04 and LAAG 4.20 do not, and those two are exactly the levels the borne-risk rows carry. Darkened to just over the floor, so the association with the badge survives: two of the four are unchanged. The lint holds every entry here to 4.5 on white, so this stays a property and not a one-off measurement.
